content.english: ℣. O Lord, + open thou my lips.

content.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.english: Alleluia.

content.english: Ant. Let us adore God * Our Saviour.

content.latin: Ant. Iubilémus Deo, * Salutári nostro.
content.english: Ant. Let us adore God * Our Saviour.

content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Iubilémus Deo, * Salutári nostro.
content.english: Ant. Let us adore God * Our Saviour.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Salutári nostro.
content.english: Ant. Our Saviour.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Ant. Iubilémus Deo, * Salutári nostro.
content.english: Ant. Let us adore God * Our Saviour.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Salutári nostro.
content.english: Ant. Our Saviour.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Ant. Iubilémus Deo, * Salutári nostro.

content.latin: Consors patérni lúminis,
content.english: O Light of Light, O Day-spring bright,

content.latin: Lux ipse lucis, et dies,
content.english: Co-equal in thy Father’s light:

content.latin: Noctem canéndo rúmpimus:
content.english: Assist us, as with prayer and psalm

content.latin: Assíste postulántibus.
content.english: Thy servants break the twilight calm.

content.latin: Aufer ténebras méntium,
content.english: All darkness from our minds dispel,

content.latin: Fuga catérvas dǽmonum,
content.english: And turn to flight the hosts of hell:

content.latin: Expélle somnoléntiam,
content.english: Bid sleepfulness our eyelids fly,

content.latin: Ne pigritántes óbruat.
content.english: Lest overwhelmed in sloth we lie.

content.latin: Sic, Christe, nobis ómnibus
content.english: Jesu, thy pardon, kind and free,

content.latin: Indúlgeas credéntibus,
content.english: Bestow on us who trust in thee:

content.latin: Ut prosit exorántibus,
content.english: And as thy praises we declare,

content.latin: Quod præcinéntes psállimus.
content.english: O with acceptance hear our prayer.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: O Father, that we ask be done,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.

content.latin: Ant. Expúgna, Dómine, * impugnántes me.
content.english: Ant. Overthrow, O Lord, * them that fight against me.

content.latin: 34:1 Iúdica, Dómine, nocéntes me, * expúgna impugnántes me.
content.english: 34:1 Judge thou, O Lord, them that wrong me: * overthrow them that fight against me.

content.latin: 34:2 Apprehénde arma et scutum: * et exsúrge in adiutórium mihi.
content.english: 34:2 Take hold of arms and shield: * and rise up to help me.

content.latin: 34:3 Effúnde frámeam, et conclúde advérsus eos, qui persequúntur me: * dic ánimæ meæ: Salus tua ego sum.
content.english: 34:3 Bring out the sword, and shut up the way against them that persecute me: * say to my soul: I am thy salvation.

content.latin: 34:4 Confundántur et revereántur, * quæréntes ánimam meam.
content.english: 34:4 Let them be confounded and ashamed * that seek after my soul.

content.latin: 34:4 Avertántur retrórsum, et confundántur * cogitántes mihi mala.
content.english: 34:4 Let them be turned back and be confounded * that devise against me.

content.latin: 34:5 Fiant tamquam pulvis ante fáciem venti: * et Ángelus Dómini coárctans eos.
content.english: 34:5 Let them become as dust before the wind: * and let the Angel of the Lord straiten them.

content.latin: 34:6 Fiat via illórum ténebræ et lúbricum: * et Ángelus Dómini pérsequens eos.
content.english: 34:6 Let their way become dark and slippery; * and let the Angel of the Lord pursue them.

content.latin: 34:7 Quóniam gratis abscondérunt mihi intéritum láquei sui: * supervácue exprobravérunt ánimam meam.
content.english: 34:7 For without cause they have hidden their net for me unto destruction: * without cause they have upbraided my soul.

content.latin: 34:8 Véniat illi láqueus, quem ignórat: et cáptio, quam abscóndit, apprehéndat eum: * et in láqueum cadat in ipsum.
content.english: 34:8 Let the snare which he knoweth not come upon him: and let the net which he hath hidden catch him: * and into that very snare let them fall.

content.latin: 34:9 Ánima autem mea exsultábit in Dómino: * et delectábitur super salutári suo.
content.english: 34:9 But my soul shall rejoice in the Lord; * and shall be delighted in his salvation.

content.latin: 34:10 Ómnia ossa mea dicent: * Dómine, quis símilis tibi?
content.english: 34:10 All my bones shall say: * Lord, who is like to thee?

content.latin: 34:10 Erípiens ínopem de manu fortiórum eius: * egénum et páuperem a diripiéntibus eum.
content.english: 34:10 Who deliverest the poor from the hand of them that are stronger than he; * the needy and the poor from them that strip him.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Expúgna, Dómine, impugnántes me.
content.english: Ant. Overthrow, O Lord, them that fight against me.

content.latin: Ant. Restítue ánimam meam * a malefáctis eórum, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. Rescue, O Lord, * my soul from their malice.

content.latin: 34:11 Surgéntes testes iníqui, * quæ ignorábam interrogábant me.
content.english: 34:11 Unjust witnesses rising up * have asked me things I knew not.

content.latin: 34:12 Retribuébant mihi mala pro bonis: * sterilitátem ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 34:12 They repaid me evil for good: * to the depriving me of my soul.

content.latin: 34:13 Ego autem cum mihi molésti essent, * induébar cilício.
content.english: 34:13 But as for me, when they were troublesome to me, * I was clothed with haircloth.

content.latin: 34:13 Humiliábam in ieiúnio ánimam meam: * et orátio mea in sinu meo convertétur.
content.english: 34:13 I humbled my soul with fasting; * and my prayer shall be turned into my bosom.

content.latin: 34:14 Quasi próximum, et quasi fratrem nostrum, sic complacébam: * quasi lugens et contristátus, sic humiliábar.
content.english: 34:14 As a neighbour and as an own brother, so did I please: * as one mourning and sorrowful so was I humbled.

content.latin: 34:15 Et advérsum me lætáti sunt, et convenérunt: * congregáta sunt super me flagélla, et ignorávi.
content.english: 34:15 But they rejoiced against me, and came together: * scourges were gathered together upon me, and I knew not.

content.latin: 34:16 Dissipáti sunt, nec compúncti, tentavérunt me, subsannavérunt me subsannatióne: * frenduérunt super me déntibus suis.
content.english: 34:16 They were separated, and repented not: they tempted me, they scoffed at me with scorn: * they gnashed upon me with their teeth.

content.latin: 34:17 Dómine, quando respícies? * restítue ánimam meam a malignitáte eórum, a leónibus únicam meam.
content.english: 34:17 Lord, when wilt thou look upon me? * rescue thou my soul from their malice: my only one from the lions.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Restítue ánimam meam a malefáctis eórum, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. Rescue, O Lord, my soul from their malice.

content.latin: Ant. Exsúrge, Dómine, * et inténde iudício meo.
content.english: Ant. Arise, O Lord, * and be attentive to my judgment.

content.latin: 34:18 Confitébor tibi in ecclésia magna, * in pópulo gravi laudábo te.
content.english: 34:18 I will give thanks to thee in a great church; * I will praise thee in a strong people.

content.latin: 34:19 Non supergáudeant mihi qui adversántur mihi iníque: * qui odérunt me gratis et ánnuunt óculis.
content.english: 34:19 Let not them that are my enemies wrongfully rejoice over me: * who have hated me without cause, and wink with the eyes.

content.latin: 34:20 Quóniam mihi quidem pacífice loquebántur: * et in iracúndia terræ loquéntes, dolos cogitábant.
content.english: 34:20 For they spoke indeed peaceably to me; * and speaking in the anger of the earth they devised guile.

content.latin: 34:21 Et dilatavérunt super me os suum: * dixérunt: Euge, euge, vidérunt óculi nostri.
content.english: 34:21 And they opened their mouth wide against me; * they said: Well done, well done, our eyes have seen it.

content.latin: 34:22 Vidísti, Dómine, ne síleas: * Dómine, ne discédas a me.
content.english: 34:22 Thou hast seen, O Lord, be not thou silent: * O Lord, depart not from me.

content.latin: 34:23 Exsúrge et inténde iudício meo: * Deus meus, et Dóminus meus in causam meam.
content.english: 34:23 Arise, and be attentive to my judgment: * to my cause, my God, and my Lord.

content.latin: 34:24 Iúdica me secúndum iustítiam tuam, Dómine, Deus meus, * et non supergáudeant mihi.
content.english: 34:24 Judge me, O Lord my God according to thy justice, * and let them not rejoice over me.

content.latin: 34:25 Non dicant in córdibus suis: Euge, euge, ánimæ nostræ: * nec dicant: Devorávimus eum.
content.english: 34:25 Let them not say in their hearts: It is well, it is well, to our mind: * neither let them say: We have swallowed him up.

content.latin: 34:26 Erubéscant et revereántur simul, * qui gratulántur malis meis.
content.english: 34:26 Let them blush: and be ashamed together, * who rejoice at my evils.

content.latin: 34:26 Induántur confusióne et reveréntia * qui magna loquúntur super me.
content.english: 34:26 Let them be clothed with confusion and shame, * who speak great things against me.

content.latin: 34:27 Exsúltent et læténtur qui volunt iustítiam meam: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus qui volunt pacem servi eius.
content.english: 34:27 Let them rejoice and be glad, who are well pleased with my justice, * and let them say always: The Lord be magnified, who delights in the peace of his servant.

content.latin: 34:28 Et lingua mea meditábitur iustítiam tuam, * tota die laudem tuam.
content.english: 34:28 And my tongue shall meditate thy justice, * thy praise all the day long.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Exsúrge, Dómine, et inténde iudício meo.
content.english: Ant. Arise, O Lord, and be attentive to my judgment.

content.latin: Ant. Noli æmulári * in eo qui prosperátur et facit iniquitátem.
content.english: Ant. Envy not * the man who prospereth in his way; the man who doth unjust things.

content.latin: 36:1 Noli æmulári in malignántibus: * neque zeláveris faciéntes iniquitátem.
content.english: 36:1 Be not emulous of evildoers; * nor envy them that work iniquity.

content.latin: 36:2 Quóniam tamquam fænum velóciter aréscent: * et quemádmodum ólera herbárum cito décident.
content.english: 36:2 For they shall shortly wither away as grass, * and as the green herbs shall quickly fall.

content.latin: 36:3 Spera in Dómino, et fac bonitátem: * et inhábita terram, et pascéris in divítiis eius.
content.english: 36:3 Trust in the Lord, and do good, * and dwell in the land, and thou shalt be fed with its riches.

content.latin: 36:4 Delectáre in Dómino: * et dabit tibi petitiónes cordis tui.
content.english: 36:4 Delight in the Lord, * and he will give thee the requests of thy heart.

content.latin: 36:5 Revéla Dómino viam tuam, et spera in eo: * et ipse fáciet.
content.english: 36:5 Commit thy way to the Lord, and trust in him, * and he will do it.

content.latin: 36:6 Et edúcet quasi lumen iustítiam tuam: et iudícium tuum tamquam merídiem: * súbditus esto Dómino, et ora eum.
content.english: 36:6 And he will bring forth thy justice as the light, and thy judgment as the noonday: * be subject to the Lord and pray to him.

content.latin: 36:7 Noli æmulári in eo, qui prosperátur in via sua: * in hómine faciénte iniustítias.
content.english: 36:7 Envy not the man who prospereth in his way; * the man who doth unjust things.

content.latin: 36:8 Désine ab ira, et derelínque furórem: * noli æmulári ut malignéris.
content.english: 36:8 Cease from anger, and leave rage; * have no emulation to do evil.

content.latin: 36:9 Quóniam qui malignántur, exterminabúntur: * sustinéntes autem Dóminum, ipsi hereditábunt terram.
content.english: 36:9 For the evildoers shall be cut off: * but they that wait upon the Lord shall inherit the land.

content.latin: 36:10 Et adhuc pusíllum, et non erit peccátor: * et quæres locum eius et non invénies.
content.english: 36:10 For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be: * and thou shalt seek his place, and shalt not find it.

content.latin: 36:11 Mansuéti autem hereditábunt terram: * et delectabúntur in multitúdine pacis.
content.english: 36:11 But the meek shall inherit the land, * and shall delight in abundance of peace.

content.latin: 36:12 Observábit peccátor iustum: * et stridébit super eum déntibus suis.
content.english: 36:12 The sinner shall watch the just man: * and shall gnash upon him with his teeth.

content.latin: 36:13 Dóminus autem irridébit eum: * quóniam próspicit quod véniet dies eius.
content.english: 36:13 But the Lord shall laugh at him: * for he foreseeth that his day shall come.

content.latin: 36:14 Gládium evaginavérunt peccatóres: * intendérunt arcum suum,
content.english: 36:14 The wicked have drawn out the sword: * they have bent their bow.

content.latin: 36:14 Ut deíciant páuperem et ínopem: * ut trucídent rectos corde.
content.english: 36:14 To cast down the poor and needy, * to kill the upright of heart.

content.latin: 36:15 Gládius eórum intret in corda ipsórum: * et arcus eórum confringátur.
content.english: 36:15 Let their sword enter into their own hearts, * and let their bow be broken.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Noli æmulári in eo qui prosperátur et facit iniquitátem.
content.english: Ant. Envy not the man who prospereth in his way; the man who doth unjust things.

content.latin: Ant. Brácchia peccatórum * conteréntur, confírmat autem iustos Dóminus.
content.english: Ant. The arms of the wicked * shall be broken in pieces; but the Lord strengtheneth the just.

content.latin: 36:16 Mélius est módicum iusto, * super divítias peccatórum multas.
content.english: 36:16 Better is a little to the just, * than the great riches of the wicked.

content.latin: 36:17 Quóniam brácchia peccatórum conteréntur: * confírmat autem iustos Dóminus.
content.english: 36:17 For the arms of the wicked shall be broken in pieces; * but the Lord strengtheneth the just.

content.latin: 36:18 Novit Dóminus dies immaculatórum: * et heréditas eórum in ætérnum erit.
content.english: 36:18 The Lord knoweth the days of the undefiled; * and their inheritance shall be for ever.

content.latin: 36:19 Non confundéntur in témpore malo, et in diébus famis saturabúntur: * quia peccatóres períbunt.
content.english: 36:19 They shall not be confounded in the evil time; and in the days of famine they shall be filled, * because the wicked shall perish.

content.latin: 36:20 Inimíci vero Dómini mox ut honorificáti fúerint et exaltáti: * deficiéntes, quemádmodum fumus defícient.
content.english: 36:20 And the enemies of the Lord, presently after they shall be honoured and exalted, * shall come to nothing and vanish like smoke.

content.latin: 36:21 Mutuábitur peccátor, et non solvet: * iustus autem miserétur et tríbuet.
content.english: 36:21 The sinner shall borrow, and not pay again; * but the just sheweth mercy and shall give.

content.latin: 36:22 Quia benedicéntes ei hereditábunt terram: * maledicéntes autem ei disperíbunt.
content.english: 36:22 For such as bless him shall inherit the land: * but such as curse him shall perish.

content.latin: 36:23 Apud Dóminum gressus hóminis dirigéntur: * et viam eius volet.
content.english: 36:23 With the Lord shall the steps of a man be directed, * and he shall like well his way.

content.latin: 36:24 Cum cecíderit non collidétur: * quia Dóminus suppónit manum suam.
content.english: 36:24 When he shall fall he shall not be bruised, * for the Lord putteth his hand under him.

content.latin: 36:25 Iúnior fui, étenim sénui: * et non vidi iustum derelíctum, nec semen eius quærens panem.
content.english: 36:25 I have been young, and now am old; * and I have not seen the just forsaken, nor his seed seeking bread.

content.latin: 36:26 Tota die miserétur et cómmodat: * et semen illíus in benedictióne erit.
content.english: 36:26 He sheweth mercy, and lendeth all the day long; * and his seed shall be in blessing.

content.latin: 36:27 Declína a malo, et fac bonum: * et inhábita in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 36:27 Decline from evil and do good, * and dwell for ever and ever.

content.latin: 36:28 Quia Dóminus amat iudícium, et non derelínquet sanctos suos: * in ætérnum conservabúntur.
content.english: 36:28 For the Lord loveth judgment, and will not forsake his saints: * they shall be preserved for ever.

content.latin: 36:28 Iniústi puniéntur: * et semen impiórum períbit.
content.english: 36:28 The unjust shall be punished, * and the seed of the wicked shall perish.

content.latin: 36:29 Iusti autem hereditábunt terram: * et inhabitábunt in sǽculum sǽculi super eam.
content.english: 36:29 But the just shall inherit the land, * and shall dwell therein for evermore.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Brácchia peccatórum conteréntur, confírmat autem iustos Dóminus.
content.english: Ant. The arms of the wicked shall be broken in pieces; but the Lord strengtheneth the just.

content.latin: Ant. Custódi innocéntiam * et vide æquitátem.
content.english: Ant. Keep innocence * and behold justice.

content.latin: 36:30 Os iusti meditábitur sapiéntiam, * et lingua eius loquétur iudícium.
content.english: 36:30 The mouth of the just shall meditate wisdom: * and his tongue shall speak judgment.

content.latin: 36:31 Lex Dei eius in corde ipsíus, * et non supplantabúntur gressus eius.
content.english: 36:31 The law of his God is in his heart, * and his steps shall not be supplanted.

content.latin: 36:32 Consíderat peccátor iustum: * et quærit mortificáre eum.
content.english: 36:32 The wicked watcheth the just man, * and seeketh to put him to death.

content.latin: 36:33 Dóminus autem non derelínquet eum in mánibus eius: * nec damnábit eum, cum iudicábitur illi.
content.english: 36:33 But the Lord will not leave him in his hands; * nor condemn him when he shall be judged.

content.latin: 36:34 Exspécta Dóminum, et custódi viam eius: et exaltábit te ut hereditáte cápias terram: * cum períerint peccatóres vidébis.
content.english: 36:34 Expect the Lord and keep his way: and he will exalt thee to inherit the land: * when the sinners shall perish thou shalt see.

content.latin: 36:35 Vidi ímpium superexaltátum, * et elevátum sicut cedros Líbani.
content.english: 36:35 I have seen the wicked highly exalted, * and lifted up like the cedars of Libanus.

content.latin: 36:36 Et transívi, et ecce non erat: * et quæsívi eum, et non est invéntus locus eius.
content.english: 36:36 And I passed by, and lo, he was not: * and I sought him and his place was not found.

content.latin: 36:37 Custódi innocéntiam, et vide æquitátem: * quóniam sunt relíquiæ hómini pacífico.
content.english: 36:37 Keep innocence, and behold justice: * for there are remnants for the peaceable man.

content.latin: 36:38 Iniústi autem disperíbunt simul: * relíquiæ impiórum interíbunt.
content.english: 36:38 But the unjust shall be destroyed together: * the remnants of the wicked shall perish.

content.latin: 36:39 Salus autem iustórum a Dómino: * et protéctor eórum in témpore tribulatiónis.
content.english: 36:39 But the salvation of the just is from the Lord, * and he is their protector in the time of trouble.

content.latin: 36:40 Et adiuvábit eos Dóminus et liberábit eos: * et éruet eos a peccatóribus, et salvábit eos: quia speravérunt in eo.
content.english: 36:40 And the Lord will help them and deliver them: * and he will rescue them from the wicked, and save them, because they have hoped in him.

content.latin: 37:2 Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me.
content.english: 37:2 Rebuke me not, O Lord, in thy indignation; * nor chastise me in thy wrath.

content.latin: 37:3 Quóniam sagíttæ tuæ infíxæ sunt mihi: * et confirmásti super me manum tuam.
content.english: 37:3 For thy arrows are fastened in me: * and thy hand hath been strong upon me.

content.latin: 37:4 Non est sánitas in carne mea a fácie iræ tuæ: * non est pax óssibus meis a fácie peccatórum meórum.
content.english: 37:4 There is no health in my flesh, because of thy wrath: * there is no peace for my bones, because of my sins.

content.latin: 37:5 Quóniam iniquitátes meæ supergréssæ sunt caput meum: * et sicut onus grave gravátæ sunt super me.
content.english: 37:5 For my iniquities are gone over my head: * and as a heavy burden are become heavy upon me.

content.latin: 37:6 Putruérunt et corrúptæ sunt cicatríces meæ, * a fácie insipiéntiæ meæ.
content.english: 37:6 My sores are putrified and corrupted, * because of my foolishness.

content.latin: 37:7 Miser factus sum, et curvátus sum usque in finem: * tota die contristátus ingrediébar.
content.english: 37:7 I am become miserable, and am bowed down even to the end: * I walked sorrowful all the day long.

content.latin: 37:8 Quóniam lumbi mei impléti sunt illusiónibus: * et non est sánitas in carne mea.
content.english: 37:8 For my loins are filled with illusions; * and there is no health in my flesh.

content.latin: 37:9 Afflíctus sum, et humiliátus sum nimis: * rugiébam a gémitu cordis mei.
content.english: 37:9 I am afflicted and humbled exceedingly: * I roared with the groaning of my heart.

content.english: 37:10 Lord, all my desire is before thee, * and my groaning is not hidden from thee.

content.english: 37:16 For in thee, O Lord, have I hoped: * thou wilt hear me, O Lord my God.

content.english: 37:17 For I said: Lest at any time my enemies rejoice over me: * and whilst my feet are moved, they speak great things against me.

content.english: 37:18 For I am ready for scourges: * and my sorrow is continually before me.

content.english: 37:20 But my enemies live, and are stronger than I: * and they that hate me wrongfully are multiplied.

content.english: 37:21 They that render evil for good, have detracted me, * because I followed goodness.

content.latin: 38:5 Locútus sum in lingua mea: * Notum fac mihi, Dómine, finem meum.
content.english: 38:5 I spoke with my tongue: * O Lord, make me know my end.

content.latin: 38:5 Et númerum diérum meórum quis est: * ut sciam quid desit mihi.
content.english: 38:5 And what is the number of my days: * that I may know what is wanting to me.

content.english: 38:6 Behold thou hast made my days measurable: * and my substance is as nothing before thee.

content.latin: 38:6 Verúmtamen univérsa vánitas, * omnis homo vivens.

content.english: 38:8 And now what is my hope? Is it not the Lord? * And my substance is with thee.

content.latin: 38:9 Ab ómnibus iniquitátibus meis érue me: * oppróbrium insipiénti dedísti me.
content.english: 38:9 Deliver thou me from all my iniquities: * thou hast made me a reproach to the fool.

content.english: 38:12 The strength of thy hand hath made me faint in rebukes: * thou hast corrected man for iniquity.

content.english: 38:12 And thou hast made his soul to waste away like a spider: * surely in vain is any man disquieted.

content.latin: 38:13 Exáudi oratiónem meam, Dómine, et deprecatiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe lácrimas meas.
content.english: 38:13 Hear my prayer, O Lord, and my supplication: * give ear to my tears.

content.latin: Fuit in diébus Heródis, regis Iudǽæ, sacérdos quidam, nómine Zacharías, de vice Abía et uxor illíus de filiábus Aaron, et nomen eius Elísabeth. Et réliqua.

content.latin: Liber 1 in Lucam
content.english: Bk. i. on Luke

content.latin: Docet nos Scriptúra divína non solum mores in iis qui prædicábiles sunt, sed étiam paréntes oportére laudári; ut véluti transmíssa immaculátæ puritátis heréditas, in iis quos vólumus laudáre, præcéllat. Quæ enim ália inténtio hoc loco sancti Evangelístæ, nisi ut sanctus Ioánnes Baptísta nobilitétur paréntibus, miráculis, móribus, múnere, passióne? Sic étiam sancti Sámuel mater Anna laudátur; sic Isaac a paréntibus nobilitátem pietátis accépit, quam pósteris derelíquit. Sacérdos ítaque Zacharías, nec solum sacérdos, sed étiam de vice Abía, id est, nóbilis inter superióres famílias.
content.english: The Divine Scriptures teach us that we are behoven to praise the lives, not only of those concerning whom we are to speak honourably, but the lives also of their fathers, so as to show that that which we will praise in our subjects was in them a gift inherited from the bright purity of the source from which they came. What other meaning can the holy Evangelist have had in this place but to glorify St. John the Baptist, as well for having been the offspring of such parents, as for his miracles, his life, his gifts, and his sufferings? So likewise is praise ascribed to Hannah, the mother of Samuel so also did Isaac draw from his parents that noble godliness which he in his turn bequeathed to his children. Thus it is told not only that Zacharias was a Priest, but a Priest of the course of Abia, that is to say, of a family noble among the noblest.

content.latin: Et uxor, inquit, illi de filiábus Aaron. Non solum ígitur a paréntibus, sed étiam a maióribus sancti Ioánnis nobílitas propagátur, non sæculári potestáte sublímis, sed religiónis successióne venerábilis. Tales enim maióres habére débuit prænúntius Christi; ut non repénte concéptam, sed a maióribus accéptam et ipso infúsam iure natúræ, prædicáre fidem Domínici viderétur advéntus. Erant, inquit, ambo iusti ante Deum, incedéntes in ómnibus mandátis et iustificatiónibus Dómini sine queréla. Quid ad hoc réferunt qui, peccátis suis solátia præferéntes, sine peccátis frequéntibus hóminem putant esse non posse; et utúntur versículo, quia scriptum est in Iob: Nemo mundus a sorde, nec si uníus diéi vita eius sit in terra?
content.english: And his wife was of the daughters of Aaron. Thus we see that the noble blood of St. John was inherited not only from parents, but from an ancient ancestry, not illustrious indeed by worldly power, but worshipful for the tradition of a sacred succession. Such were the forefathers whom it well became the Fore-runner of the Christ to have, that it might manifestly fall to his lot, not as a sudden gift, but as an heir-loom, to preach belief in the coming of the Lord. And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord, blameless. What do they make of this text who, to take them some consolation for their own sins, hold that man cannot exist without oftentimes sinning, and quote to that end that which is written in Job: Not one is clean, even though his life on the earth be but one day?

content.latin: Quibus respondéndum est, prius ut quid sit hóminem sine peccáto esse defíniant: utrum nunquam omníno peccásse, an desiísse peccáre. Si enim hoc putant sine peccáto esse, nunquam omníno peccásse; et ipse conséntio. Omnes enim peccavérunt, et egent glória Dei. Sin autem eum qui véterem errórem corréxerit, et in eam se vitæ transformáverit qualitátem, ut témperet a peccáto, negant abstinére a delíctis; non possum in eórum conveníre senténtiam, cum legámus, quia Sic Dóminus diléxit Ecclésiam, ut exhíbeat ipsam sibi gloriósam, et non habéntem máculam, aut rugam, aut áliquid eiúsmodi; sed ut sit sancta et immaculáta.
content.english: To such we must reply by asking them first to tell us what they mean by a man without sin whether it be one who hath never sinned, or one who hath ceased to sin. If they mean by a man without sin one who hath never sinned, I myself agree in their position, for all have sinned and come short of the glory of God. Rom. iii. 23. But if they mean to deny that he who hath reformed his old crooked ways, and changed his life for a new one, on purpose to avoid sin, cannot avoid sin, I am not able to subscribe to their opinion while I read that Christ loved the Church and gave Himself for it, that He might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, that He might present it to Himself a glorious Church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing but that it should be holy and without blemish. Eph. v. 25-27.

content.english: ℟. Thus saith the Lord: I took thee out of thy father's house, and appointed thee to be ruler over My people, over Israel.

content.latin: * Et fui tecum in ómnibus ubicúmque ambulásti, firmans regnum tuum in ætérnum.
content.english: * And I was with thee whithersoever thou wentest, to establish thy kingdom for ever.

content.latin: ℣. Fecíque tibi nomen grande, iuxta nomen magnórum, qui sunt in terra: et réquiem dedi tibi ab ómnibus inimícis tuis.
content.english: ℣. And I have made thee a great name, like unto the name of the great men that are in the earth and have caused thee to rest from all thine enemies.

content.latin: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut família tua per viam salútis incédat; et beáti Ioánnis Præcursóris hortaménta sectándo, ad eum quem prædíxit, secúra pervéniat, Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum:
content.english: Grant, we beseech Thee, O Lord, unto this Thy family the grace to walk always in the path of salvation, that they, obediently following the exhortation of the blessed Fore-runner John, may at the last attain safely unto Him Whom John heralded, Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord:

content.latin: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Who with thee liveth and reigneth, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.

content.latin: Psalmus 50 [1]
content.english: Psalm 50 [1]

content.latin: 50:3 Miserére mei, Deus, * secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam.
content.english: 50:3 Have mercy on me, O God, * according to thy great mercy.

content.latin: 50:3 Et secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum, * dele iniquitátem meam.
content.english: 50:3 And according to the multitude of thy tender mercies * blot out my iniquity.

content.latin: 50:4 Ámplius lava me ab iniquitáte mea: * et a peccáto meo munda me.
content.english: 50:4 Wash me yet more from my iniquity, * and cleanse me from my sin.

content.latin: 50:5 Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco: * et peccátum meum contra me est semper.
content.english: 50:5 For I know my iniquity, * and my sin is always before me.

content.latin: 50:6 Tibi soli peccávi, et malum coram te feci: * ut iustificéris in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum iudicáris.
content.english: 50:6 To thee only have I sinned, and have done evil before thee: * that thou mayst be justified in thy words, and mayst overcome when thou art judged.

content.latin: 50:7 Ecce enim, in iniquitátibus concéptus sum: * et in peccátis concépit me mater mea.
content.english: 50:7 For behold I was conceived in iniquities; * and in sins did my mother conceive me.

content.latin: 50:8 Ecce enim, veritátem dilexísti: * incérta et occúlta sapiéntiæ tuæ manifestásti mihi.
content.english: 50:8 For behold thou hast loved truth: * the uncertain and hidden things of thy wisdom thou hast made manifest to me.

content.latin: 50:9 Aspérges me hyssópo, et mundábor: * lavábis me, et super nivem dealbábor.
content.english: 50:9 Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed: * thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.

content.latin: 50:10 Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam: * et exsultábunt ossa humiliáta.
content.english: 50:10 To my hearing thou shalt give joy and gladness: * and the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

content.latin: 50:11 Avérte fáciem tuam a peccátis meis: * et omnes iniquitátes meas dele.
content.english: 50:11 Turn away thy face from my sins, * and blot out all my iniquities.

content.latin: 50:12 Cor mundum crea in me, Deus: * et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.
content.english: 50:12 Create a clean heart in me, O God: * and renew a right spirit within my bowels.

content.latin: 50:13 Ne proícias me a fácie tua: * et spíritum sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me.
content.english: 50:13 Cast me not away from thy face; * and take not thy holy spirit from me.

content.latin: 50:14 Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui: * et spíritu principáli confírma me.
content.english: 50:14 Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation, * and strengthen me with a perfect spirit.

content.latin: 50:15 Docébo iníquos vias tuas: * et ímpii ad te converténtur.
content.english: 50:15 I will teach the unjust thy ways: * and the wicked shall be converted to thee.

content.latin: 50:16 Líbera me de sanguínibus, Deus, Deus salútis meæ: * et exsultábit lingua mea iustítiam tuam.
content.english: 50:16 Deliver me from blood, O God, thou God of my salvation: * and my tongue shall extol thy justice.

content.latin: 50:17 Dómine, lábia mea apéries: * et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
content.english: 50:17 O Lord, thou wilt open my lips: * and my mouth shall declare thy praise.

content.latin: 50:18 Quóniam si voluísses sacrifícium, dedíssem útique: * holocáustis non delectáberis.
content.english: 50:18 For if thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would indeed have given it: * with burnt offerings thou wilt not be delighted.

content.latin: 50:19 Sacrifícium Deo spíritus contribulátus: * cor contrítum, et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.
content.english: 50:19 A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: * a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

content.latin: 50:20 Benígne fac, Dómine, in bona voluntáte tua Sion: * ut ædificéntur muri Ierúsalem.
content.english: 50:20 Deal favourably, O Lord, in thy good will with Sion; * that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up.

content.latin: 50:21 Tunc acceptábis sacrifícium iustítiæ, oblatiónes, et holocáusta: * tunc impónent super altáre tuum vítulos.
content.english: 50:21 Then shalt thou accept the sacrifice of justice, oblations and whole burnt offerings: * then shall they lay calves upon thy altar.

content.latin: Psalmus 42 [2]
content.english: Psalm 42 [2]

content.latin: 42:1 Iúdica me, Deus, et discérne causam meam de gente non sancta, * ab hómine iníquo, et dolóso érue me.
content.english: 42:1 Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from the nation that is not holy: * deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.

content.latin: 42:2 Quia tu es, Deus, fortitúdo mea: * quare me repulísti? et quare tristis incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
content.english: 42:2 For thou art God my strength: * why hast thou cast me off? and why do I go sorrowful whilst the enemy afflicteth me?

content.latin: 42:3 Emítte lucem tuam et veritátem tuam: * ipsa me deduxérunt, et adduxérunt in montem sanctum tuum, et in tabernácula tua.
content.english: 42:3 Send forth thy light and thy truth: * they have conducted me, and brought me unto thy holy hill, and into thy tabernacles.

content.latin: 42:4 Et introíbo ad altáre Dei: * ad Deum, qui lætíficat iuventútem meam.
content.english: 42:4 And I will go in to the altar of God: * to God who giveth joy to my youth.

content.latin: 42:5 Confitébor tibi in cíthara, Deus, Deus meus: * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 42:5 To thee, O God my God, I will give praise upon the harp: * why art thou sad, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

content.latin: 42:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 42:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

content.latin: 66:2 Deus misereátur nostri, et benedícat nobis: * ‡ illúminet vultum suum super nos, et misereátur nostri.
content.english: 66:2 May God have mercy on us, and bless us: * ‡ may he cause the light of his countenance to shine upon us, and may he have mercy on us.

content.latin: 66:3 Ut cognoscámus in terra viam tuam, * in ómnibus géntibus salutáre tuum.
content.english: 66:3 That we may know thy way upon earth: * thy salvation in all nations.

content.latin: 66:4 Confiteántur tibi pópuli, Deus: * confiteántur tibi pópuli omnes.
content.english: 66:4 Let people confess to thee, O God: * let all people give praise to thee.

content.latin: 66:5 Læténtur et exsúltent gentes: * quóniam iúdicas pópulos in æquitáte, et gentes in terra dírigis.
content.english: 66:5 Let the nations be glad and rejoice: * for thou judgest the people with justice, and directest the nations upon earth.

content.latin: 66:6 Confiteántur tibi pópuli, Deus, confiteántur tibi pópuli omnes: * terra dedit fructum suum.
content.english: 66:6 Let the people, O God, confess to thee: * let all the people give praise to thee: the earth hath yielded her fruit.

content.latin: 66:7 Benedícat nos Deus, Deus noster, benedícat nos Deus: * et métuant eum omnes fines terræ.
content.english: 66:7 May God, our God bless us, may God bless us: * and all the ends of the earth fear him.

content.latin: 38:10 Ego dixi: In dimídio diérum meórum * vadam ad portas ínferi.
content.english: 38:10 I said: In the midst of my days * I shall go to the gates of hell:

content.latin: 38:11 Quæsívi resíduum annórum meórum. * Dixi: Non vidébo Dóminum Deum in terra vivéntium.
content.english: 38:11 I sought for the residue of my years. * I said: I shall not see the Lord God in the land of the living.

content.latin: 38:12 Non aspíciam hóminem ultra, * et habitatórem quiétis.
content.english: 38:12 I shall behold man no more, * nor the inhabitant of rest.

content.latin: 38:13 Generátio mea abláta est, et convolúta est a me, * quasi tabernáculum pastórum.
content.english: 38:13 My generation is at an end, and it is rolled away from me, * as a shepherd’s tent.

content.latin: 38:14 Præcísa est velut a texénte, vita mea: dum adhuc ordírer, succídit me: * de mane usque ad vésperam fínies me.
content.english: 38:14 My life is cut off, as by a weaver: whilst I was yet but beginning, he cut me off: * from morning even to night thou wilt make an end of me.

content.latin: 38:15 Sperábam usque ad mane, * quasi leo sic contrívit ómnia ossa mea:
content.english: 38:15 I hoped till morning, * as a lion so hath he broken all my bones:

content.latin: 38:16 De mane usque ad vésperam fínies me: * sicut pullus hirúndinis sic clamábo, meditábor ut colúmba:
content.english: 38:16 From morning even to night thou wilt make an end of me. * I will cry like a young swallow, I will meditate like a dove:

content.latin: 38:17 Attenuáti sunt óculi mei, * suspiciéntes in excélsum.
content.english: 38:17 My eyes are weakened * looking upward:

content.latin: 38:18 Dómine, vim pátior, respónde pro me. * Quid dicam, aut quid respondébit mihi, cum ipse fécerit?
content.english: 38:18 Lord, I suffer violence, answer thou for me. * What shall I say, or what shall he answer for me, whereas he himself hath done it?

content.latin: 38:19 Recogitábo tibi omnes annos meos * in amaritúdine ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 38:19 I will recount to thee all my years * in the bitterness of my soul.

content.latin: 38:20 Dómine, si sic vívitur, et in tálibus vita spíritus mei, corrípies me, et vivificábis me. * Ecce, in pace amaritúdo mea amaríssima:
content.english: 38:20 O Lord, if man’s life be such, and the life of my spirit be in such things as these, thou shalt correct me, and make me to live. * Behold in peace is my bitterness most bitter:

content.latin: 38:21 Tu autem eruísti ánimam meam ut non períret: * proiecísti post tergum tuum ómnia peccáta mea.
content.english: 38:21 But thou hast delivered my soul that it should not perish, * thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back.

content.latin: 38:22 Quia non inférnus confitébitur tibi, neque mors laudábit te: * non exspectábunt qui descéndunt in lacum, veritátem tuam.
content.english: 38:22 For hell shall not confess to thee, neither shall death praise thee: * nor shall they that go down into the pit, look for thy truth.

content.latin: 38:23 Vivens vivens ipse confitébitur tibi, sicut et ego hódie: * pater fíliis notam fáciet veritátem tuam.
content.english: 38:23 The living, the living, he shall give praise to thee, as I do this day: * the father shall make thy truth known to the children.

content.latin: 38:24 Dómine, salvum me fac * et psalmos nostros cantábimus cunctis diébus vitæ nostræ in domo Dómini.
content.english: 38:24 O Lord, save me, and we will sing our psalms all the days of our life * in the house of the Lord.

content.latin: Psalmus 134 [5]
content.english: Psalm 134 [5]

content.latin: 134:1 Laudáte nomen Dómini, * laudáte, servi, Dóminum.
content.english: 134:1 Praise ye the name of the Lord: * O you his servants, praise the Lord:

content.latin: 134:2 Qui statis in domo Dómini, * in átriis domus Dei nostri.
content.english: 134:2 You that stand in the house of the Lord, * in the courts of the house of our God.

content.latin: 134:3 Laudáte Dóminum, quia bonus Dóminus: * psállite nómini eius, quóniam suáve.
content.english: 134:3 Praise ye the Lord, for the Lord is good: * sing ye to his name, for it is sweet.

content.latin: 134:4 Quóniam Iacob elégit sibi Dóminus, * Israël in possessiónem sibi.
content.english: 134:4 For the Lord hath chosen Jacob unto himself: * Israel for his own possession.

content.latin: 134:5 Quia ego cognóvi quod magnus est Dóminus, * et Deus noster præ ómnibus diis.
content.english: 134:5 For I have known that the Lord is great, * and our God is above all gods.

content.latin: 134:6 Ómnia quæcúmque vóluit, Dóminus fecit in cælo, et in terra, * in mari, et in ómnibus abýssis.
content.english: 134:6 Whatsoever the Lord pleased he hath done, in heaven, in earth, * in the sea, and in all the deeps.

content.latin: 134:7 Edúcens nubes ab extrémo terræ: * fúlgura in plúviam fecit.
content.english: 134:7 He bringeth up clouds from the end of the earth: * he hath made lightnings for the rain.

content.latin: 134:8 Qui prodúcit ventos de thesáuris suis: * qui percússit primogénita Ægýpti ab hómine usque ad pecus.
content.english: 134:8 He bringeth forth winds out of his stores: * He slew the firstborn of Egypt from man even unto beast.

content.latin: 134:9 Et misit signa, et prodígia in médio tui, Ægýpte: * in Pharaónem, et in omnes servos eius.
content.english: 134:9 He sent forth signs and wonders in the midst of thee, O Egypt: * upon Pharao, and upon all his servants.

content.latin: 134:10 Qui percússit gentes multas: * et occídit reges fortes:
content.english: 134:10 He smote many nations, * and slew mighty kings:

content.latin: 134:11 Sehon, regem Amorrhæórum, et Og, regem Basan, * et ómnia regna Chánaan.
content.english: 134:11 Sehon king of the Amorrhites, and Og king of Basan, * and all the kingdoms of Chanaan.

content.latin: 134:12 Et dedit terram eórum hereditátem, * hereditátem Israël, pópulo suo.
content.english: 134:12 And gave their land for an inheritance, * for an inheritance to his people Israel.

content.latin: 134:13 Dómine, nomen tuum in ætérnum: * Dómine, memoriále tuum in generatiónem et generatiónem.
content.english: 134:13 Thy name, O Lord, is for ever: * thy memorial, O Lord, unto all generations.

content.latin: 134:14 Quia iudicábit Dóminus pópulum suum: * et in servis suis deprecábitur.
content.english: 134:14 For the Lord will judge his people, * and will be entreated in favour of his servants.

content.latin: 134:15 Simulácra géntium argéntum, et aurum, * ópera mánuum hóminum.
content.english: 134:15 The idols of the Gentiles are silver and gold, * the works of men’s hands.

content.latin: 134:16 Os habent, et non loquéntur: * óculos habent, et non vidébunt.
content.english: 134:16 They have a mouth, but they speak not: * they have eyes, but they see not.

content.latin: 134:17 Aures habent, et non áudient: * neque enim est spíritus in ore ipsórum.
content.english: 134:17 They have ears, but they hear not: * neither is there any breath in their mouths.

content.latin: 134:18 Símiles illis fiant qui fáciunt ea: * et omnes qui confídunt in eis.
content.english: 134:18 Let them that make them be like to them: * and every one that trusteth in them.

content.latin: 134:19 Domus Israël, benedícite Dómino: * domus Aaron, benedícite Dómino.
content.english: 134:19 Bless the Lord, O house of Israel: * bless the Lord, O house of Aaron.

content.latin: 134:20 Domus Levi, benedícite Dómino: * qui timétis Dóminum, benedícite Dómino.
content.english: 134:20 Bless the Lord, O house of Levi: * you that fear the Lord, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 134:21 Benedíctus Dóminus ex Sion, * qui hábitat in Ierúsalem.
content.english: 134:21 Blessed be the Lord out of Sion, * who dwelleth in Jerusalem.

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

content.latin: Psalmus 24(1-7) [1]
24:1 Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam: * Deus meus, in te confído, non erubéscam.
content.english: 24:1 To thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul: * In thee, O my God, I put my trust; let me not be ashamed.

content.latin: 24:3 Neque irrídeant me inimíci mei: * étenim univérsi, qui sústinent te, non confundéntur.
content.english: 24:3 Neither let my enemies laugh at me: * for none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded.

content.latin: 24:4 Confundántur omnes iníqua agéntes * supervácue.
content.english: 24:4 Let all them be confounded that act unjust things * without cause.

content.latin: 24:4 Vias tuas, Dómine, demónstra mihi: * et sémitas tuas édoce me.
content.english: 24:4 Shew, O Lord, thy ways to me, * and teach me thy paths.

content.latin: 24:5 Dírige me in veritáte tua, et doce me: * quia tu es, Deus, salvátor meus, et te sustínui tota die.
content.english: 24:5 Direct me in thy truth, and teach me; * for thou art God my Saviour; and on thee have I waited all the day long.

content.latin: 24:6 Reminíscere miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, * et misericordiárum tuárum, quæ a sǽculo sunt.
content.english: 24:6 Remember, O Lord, thy bowels of compassion; * and thy mercies that are from the beginning of the world.

content.latin: 24:7 Delícta iuventútis meæ, * et ignorántias meas ne memíneris.
content.english: 24:7 The sins of my youth * and my ignorances do not remember.

content.latin: 24:7 Secúndum misericórdiam tuam meménto mei tu: * propter bonitátem tuam, Dómine.
content.english: 24:7 According to thy mercy remember thou me: * for thy goodness’ sake, O Lord.

content.latin: 24:8 Dulcis et rectus Dóminus: * propter hoc legem dabit delinquéntibus in via.
content.english: 24:8 The Lord is sweet and righteous: * therefore he will give a law to sinners in the way.

content.latin: 24:9 Díriget mansuétos in iudício: * docébit mites vias suas.
content.english: 24:9 He will guide the mild in judgment: * he will teach the meek his ways.

content.latin: 24:10 Univérsæ viæ Dómini, misericórdia et véritas, * requiréntibus testaméntum eius et testimónia eius.
content.english: 24:10 All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth, * to them that seek after his covenant and his testimonies.

content.latin: 24:11 Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, propitiáberis peccáto meo: * multum est enim.

content.english: The morrow is the birthday of the holy Baptist John, the Forerunner of the Lord, the son of Zacharias and Elizabeth, who was filled with the Holy Ghost while yet he was in his mother's womb.

content.english: June 24th 2026, the 9th day of the Moon, is made the commemoration of

content.latin: Romæ commemorátio sanctórum plurimórum Mártyrum, qui a Neróne Imperatóre, ut a se incénsæ Urbis ódium avérteret, calumnióse accusáti, divérso mortis génere iussi sunt sævíssime intérfici. Horum síquidem álii, ferárum tergis contécti, laniátibus canum expósiti sunt; álii crúcibus affíxi; aliíque incéndio tráditi, ut, ubi defecísset dies, in usum noctúrni lúminis deservírent. Erant hi omnes Apostolórum discípuli, et primítiæ Mártyrum, quas Romána Ecclésia, fértilis ager Mártyrum, ante Apostolórum necem transmísit ad Dóminum.
content.english: The very many holy martyrs at Rome who were falsely accused by the Emperor Nero of having set the city on fire, and were by him ordered to be put to death in many diverse and most cruel ways.

content.latin: Item Romæ sanctórum Mártyrum Fausti et aliórum vigínti trium.
content.english: Some were sewn up in the skins of wild beasts and put to be torn by dogs, some were crucified, some were burnt as torches to give light by night these were all disciples of the Apostles, and the first martyrs whom the Church of Rome, a field fruitful in martyrs, sent to be with the Lord, even before the slaying of the Apostles themselves.

content.latin: Mechlíniæ, in Brabántia, pássio sancti Rumóldi, Epíscopi Dublinénsis et Mártyris, e Scotórum Rege progéniti.
content.english: There also the holy martyrs Faustus and twenty-three others.

content.latin: Sátalis, in Arménia, sanctórum Mártyrum septem fratrum, scílicet Oréntii, Heróis, Pharnácii, Firmíni, Firmi, Cyríaci et Longíni mílitum; qui a Maximiáno Imperatóre, eo quod Christiáni essent, cíngulo militári priváti sunt, et, ab invícem separati atque in divérsa loca abdúcti, in dolóribus et ærúmnis pósiti, quievérunt in Dómino.
content.english: At Mechelen, in Brabant, [in the eighth century,] the holy martyr Rombout, Bishop [of that city,] son of an Irish king and Bishop of Dublin.

content.latin: In vico Christólio, in território Parisiénsi, pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Agoárdi et Aglibérti, cum áliis innúmeris promíscui sexus.
content.english: At Satala, in Armenia, the holy brethren Orentius, Eros, Pharnacius, Firminus, Firmus, Cyriacus, and Longinus, all soldiers and all martyrs. Because they were Christians, the Emperor Maximian expelled them from the army, separated them from one another, and sent them to diverse places, where in sorrow and suffering they fell asleep in the Lord, [about the year 306.]

content.latin: Augustodúni deposítio sancti Simplícii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
content.english: In the village of Créteil, in the country near Paris, the holy martyrs Agoard and Agilbert, with others, both men and women, who cannot be counted.

39:2 Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, * et inténdit mihi.
content.english: 39:2 With expectation I have waited for the Lord, * and he was attentive to me.

content.latin: 39:3 Et exaudívit preces meas: * et edúxit me de lacu misériæ, et de luto fæcis.
content.english: 39:3 And he heard my prayers, * and brought me out of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs.

content.latin: 39:3 Et státuit super petram pedes meos: * et diréxit gressus meos.
content.english: 39:3 And he set my feet upon a rock, * and directed my steps.

content.latin: 39:4 Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, * carmen Deo nostro.
content.english: 39:4 And he put a new canticle into my mouth, * a song to our God.

content.latin: 39:4 Vidébunt multi, et timébunt: * et sperábunt in Dómino.
content.english: 39:4 Many shall see, and shall fear: * and they shall hope in the Lord.

content.latin: 39:5 Beátus vir, cuius est nomen Dómini spes eius: * et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.
content.english: 39:5 Blessed is the man whose trust is in the name of the Lord; * and who hath not had regard to vanities, and lying follies.

content.latin: 39:6 Multa fecísti tu, Dómine, Deus meus, mirabília tua: * et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.
content.english: 39:6 Thou hast multiplied thy wonderful works, O Lord my God: * and in thy thoughts there is no one like to thee.

content.latin: 39:6 Annuntiávi et locútus sum: * multiplicáti sunt super númerum.
content.english: 39:6 I have declared and I have spoken * they are multiplied above number.

content.latin: 39:7 Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti: * aures autem perfecísti mihi.
content.english: 39:7 Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire; * but thou hast pierced ears for me.

content.latin: 39:7 Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti: * tunc dixi: Ecce, vénio.
content.english: 39:7 Burnt offering and sin offering thou didst not require: * then said I, Behold I come.

content.latin: 39:8 In cápite libri scriptum est de me ut fácerem voluntátem tuam: * Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei.
content.english: 39:8 In the head of the book it is written of me that I should do thy will: * O my God, I have desired it, and thy law in the midst of my heart.

content.latin: 39:10 Annuntiávi iustítiam tuam in ecclésia magna, * ecce, lábia mea non prohibébo: Dómine, tu scisti.
content.english: 39:10 I have declared thy justice in a great church, * lo, I will not restrain my lips: O Lord, thou knowest it.

content.latin: 39:11 Iustítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo: * veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.
content.english: 39:11 I have not hid thy justice within my heart: * I have declared thy truth and thy salvation.

content.latin: 39:11 Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam * a concílio multo.
content.english: 39:11 I have not concealed thy mercy and thy truth * from a great council.

content.latin: 39:12 Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: * misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.
content.english: 39:12 Withhold not thou, O Lord, thy tender mercies from me: * thy mercy and thy truth have always upheld me.

content.latin: 39:13 Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala, quorum non est númerus: * comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.
content.english: 39:13 For evils without number have surrounded me; * my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see.

content.latin: 39:13 Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: * et cor meum derelíquit me.
content.english: 39:13 They are multiplied above the hairs of my head: * and my heart hath forsaken me.

content.latin: 39:14 Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adiuvándum me réspice.
content.english: 39:14 Be pleased, O Lord to deliver me: * look down, O Lord, to help me.

content.english: 39:17 Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

content.latin: 39:18 Ego autem mendícus sum, et pauper: * Dóminus sollícitus est mei.
content.english: 39:18 But I am a beggar and poor: * the Lord is careful for me.

content.latin: 39:18 Adiútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es: * Deus meus, ne tardáveris.
content.english: 39:18 Thou art my helper and my protector: * O my God, be not slack.

content.latin: 40:2 Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.
content.english: 40:2 Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: * the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.

content.latin: 40:3 Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum eius.
content.english: 40:3 The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: * and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.

content.latin: 40:4 Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris eius: * univérsum stratum eius versásti in infirmitáte eius.
content.english: 40:4 The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: * thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.

content.latin: 40:5 Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
content.english: 40:5 I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

content.latin: 40:6 Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen eius?
content.english: 40:6 My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?

content.latin: 40:7 Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor eius congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
content.english: 40:7 And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.

content.latin: 40:7 Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
content.english: 40:7 He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.

content.latin: 40:8 Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
content.english: 40:8 All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.

content.latin: 40:9 Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
content.english: 40:9 They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?

content.latin: 40:10 Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
content.english: 40:10 For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.

content.latin: 40:11 Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
content.english: 40:11 But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.

content.latin: 40:12 In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
content.english: 40:12 By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.

content.latin: 40:13 Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
content.english: 40:13 But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

content.latin: 40:14 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.
content.english: 40:14 Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. * So be it. So be it.

41:2 Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.
content.english: 41:2 As the hart panteth after the fountains of water; * so my soul panteth after thee, O God.

content.latin: 41:3 Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?
content.english: 41:3 My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?

content.latin: 41:4 Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?
content.english: 41:4 My tears have been my bread day and night, * whilst it is said to me daily: Where is thy God?

content.latin: 41:5 In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.
content.english: 41:5 With the voice of joy and praise; * the noise of one feasting.

content.latin: 41:6 Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 41:6 Why art thou sad, O my soul? * and why dost thou trouble me?

content.latin: 41:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

content.english: 41:7 My soul is troubled within myself: * therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from the little hill.

content.english: 41:8 Deep calleth on deep, * at the noise of thy flood-gates.

content.english: 41:8 All thy heights and thy billows * have passed over me.

content.latin: 41:9 In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum eius.
content.english: 41:9 In the daytime the Lord hath commanded his mercy; * and a canticle to him in the night.

content.latin: 41:9 Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.
content.english: 41:9 With me is prayer to the God of my life. * I will say to God: Thou art my support.

content.latin: 41:10 Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
content.english: 41:10 Why hast thou forgotten me? * and why go I mourning, whilst my enemy afflicteth me?

content.latin: 41:11 Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.
content.english: 41:11 Whilst my bones are broken, * my enemies who trouble me have reproached me;

content.latin: 41:11 Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 41:11 Whilst they say to me day by day: Where is thy God? * Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

content.latin: 41:12 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:12 Hope thou in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

43:2 Deus áuribus nostris audívimus: * patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.
content.english: 43:2 We have heard, O God, with our ears: * our fathers have declared to us,

content.latin: 43:2 Opus, quod operátus es in diébus eórum, * et in diébus antíquis.
content.english: 43:2 The work thou hast wrought in their days, * and in the days of old.

content.latin: 43:3 Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.
content.english: 43:3 Thy hand destroyed the Gentiles, and thou plantedst them: * thou didst afflict the people and cast them out.

content.latin: 43:4 Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, * et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos:
content.english: 43:4 For they got not the possession of the land by their own sword: * neither did their own arm save them.

content.latin: 43:4 Sed déxtera tua, et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui: * quóniam complacuísti in eis.
content.english: 43:4 But thy right hand and thy arm, and the light of thy countenance: * because thou wast pleased with them.

content.latin: 43:5 Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus: * qui mandas salútes Iacob.
content.english: 43:5 Thou art thyself my king and my God, * who commandest the saving of Jacob.

content.latin: 43:6 In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.
content.english: 43:6 Through thee we will push down our enemies with the horn: * and through thy name we will despise them that rise up against us.

content.latin: 43:7 Non enim in arcu meo sperábo: * et gládius meus non salvábit me.
content.english: 43:7 For I will not trust in my bow: * neither shall my sword save me.

content.latin: 43:8 Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.
content.english: 43:8 But thou hast saved us from them that afflict us: * and hast put them to shame that hate us.

content.latin: 43:9 In Deo laudábimur tota die: * et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.
content.english: 43:9 In God shall we glory all the day long: * and in thy name we will give praise for ever.

content.latin: 43:10 Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos: * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.
content.english: 43:10 But now thou hast cast us off, and put us to shame: * and thou, O God, wilt not go out with our armies.

content.latin: 43:11 Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros: * et qui odérunt nos, diripiébant sibi.
content.english: 43:11 Thou hast made us turn our back to our enemies: * and they that hated us plundered for themselves.

content.latin: 43:12 Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum: * et in géntibus dispersísti nos.
content.english: 43:12 Thou hast given us up like sheep to be eaten: * thou hast scattered us among the nations.

content.latin: 43:13 Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio: * et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.
content.english: 43:13 Thou hast sold thy people for no price: * and there was no reckoning in the exchange of them.

content.latin: 43:14 Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, * subsannatiónem et derísum his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro.
content.english: 43:14 Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, * a scoff and derision to them that are round about us.

content.latin: 43:15 Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus: * commotiónem cápitis in pópulis.
content.english: 43:15 Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: * a shaking of the head among the people.

content.latin: 43:16 Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, * et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.
content.english: 43:16 All the day long my shame is before me: * and the confusion of my face hath covered me.

content.latin: 43:17 A voce exprobrántis, et obloquéntis: * a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis.
content.english: 43:17 At the voice of him that reproacheth and detracteth me: * at the face of the enemy and persecutor.

content.latin: 43:18 Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos, nec oblíti sumus te: * et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.
content.english: 43:18 All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten thee: * and we have not done wickedly in thy covenant.

content.latin: 43:19 Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum: * et declinásti sémitas nostras a via tua:
content.english: 43:19 And our heart hath not turned back: * neither hast thou turned aside our steps from thy way.

content.latin: 43:20 Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, * et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.
content.english: 43:20 For thou hast humbled us in the place of affliction: * and the shadow of death hath covered us.

content.latin: 43:21 Si oblíti sumus nomen Dei nostri, * et si expándimus manus nostras ad deum aliénum:
content.english: 43:21 If we have forgotten the name of our God, * and if we have spread forth our hands to a strange god:

content.latin: 43:22 Nonne Deus requíret ista? * ipse enim novit abscóndita cordis.
content.english: 43:22 Shall not God search out these things: * for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.

content.latin: 43:22 Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die: * æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.
content.english: 43:22 Because for thy sake we are killed all the day long: * we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

content.latin: 43:23 Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? * exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.
content.english: 43:23 Arise, why sleepest thou, O Lord? * arise, and cast us not off to the end.

content.latin: 43:24 Quare fáciem tuam avértis, * oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ, et tribulatiónis nostræ?
content.english: 43:24 Why turnest thou thy face away? * and forgettest our want and our trouble?

content.latin: 43:25 Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra: * conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.
content.english: 43:25 For our soul is humbled down to the dust: * our belly cleaveth to the earth.

content.latin: 43:26 Exsúrge, Dómine, ádiuva nos: * et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.
content.english: 43:26 Arise, O Lord, help us * and redeem us for thy name’s sake.

content.latin: 109:1 Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
content.english: 109:1 The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

content.latin: 109:1 Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
content.english: 109:1 Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

content.latin: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
content.english: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

content.latin: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
content.english: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

content.latin: 109:4 Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.

content.latin: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.

content.latin: 4:3 Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?
content.english: 4:3 O ye sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? * Why do you love vanity, and seek after lying?

content.latin: 4:4 Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.
content.english: 4:4 Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: * the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.

content.latin: 4:5 Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
content.english: 4:5 Be ye angry, and sin not: * the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds.

content.latin: 4:6 Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
content.english: 4:6 Offer up the sacrifice of justice, and trust in the Lord: * many say, Who sheweth us good things?

content.latin: 4:7 Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
content.english: 4:7 The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * thou hast given gladness in my heart.

content.latin: 4:8 A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.
content.english: 4:8 By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, * they are multiplied.

content.latin: 4:9 In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;
content.english: 4:9 In peace in the selfsame * I will sleep, and I will rest:

content.latin: 4:10 Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.
content.english: 4:10 For thou, O Lord, singularly * hast settled me in hope.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Psalmus 90 [2]
content.english: Psalm 90 [2]

content.latin: 90:1 Qui hábitat in adiutório Altíssimi, * in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.
content.english: 90:1 He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High, * shall abide under the protection of the God of Jacob.

content.latin: 90:2 Dicet Dómino: Suscéptor meus es tu, et refúgium meum: * Deus meus sperábo in eum.
content.english: 90:2 He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector, and my refuge: * my God, in him will I trust.

content.latin: 90:3 Quóniam ipse liberávit me de láqueo venántium, * et a verbo áspero.
content.english: 90:3 For he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters: * and from the sharp word.

content.latin: 90:4 Scápulis suis obumbrábit tibi: * et sub pennis eius sperábis.
content.english: 90:4 He will overshadow thee with his shoulders: * and under his wings thou shalt trust.

content.latin: 90:5 Scuto circúmdabit te véritas eius: * non timébis a timóre noctúrno,
content.english: 90:5 His truth shall compass thee with a shield: * thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night.

content.latin: 90:6 A sagítta volánte in die, a negótio perambulánte in ténebris: * ab incúrsu, et dæmónio meridiáno.
content.english: 90:6 Of the arrow that flieth in the day, of the business that walketh about in the dark: * of invasion, or of the noonday devil.

content.latin: 90:7 Cadent a látere tuo mille, et decem míllia a dextris tuis: * ad te autem non appropinquábit.
content.english: 90:7 A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand: * but it shall not come nigh thee.

content.latin: 90:8 Verúmtamen óculis tuis considerábis: * et retributiónem peccatórum vidébis.
content.english: 90:8 But thou shalt consider with thy eyes: * and shalt see the reward of the wicked.

content.latin: 90:9 Quóniam tu es, Dómine, spes mea: * Altíssimum posuísti refúgium tuum.
content.english: 90:9 Because thou, O Lord, art my hope: * thou hast made the most High thy refuge.

content.latin: 90:10 Non accédet ad te malum: * et flagéllum non appropinquábit tabernáculo tuo.
content.english: 90:10 There shall no evil come to thee: * nor shall the scourge come near thy dwelling.

content.latin: 90:11 Quóniam Ángelis suis mandávit de te: * ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
content.english: 90:11 For he hath given his angels charge over thee; * to keep thee in all thy ways.

content.latin: 90:12 In mánibus portábunt te: * ne forte offéndas ad lápidem pedem tuum.
content.english: 90:12 In their hands they shall bear thee up: * lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.

content.latin: 90:13 Super áspidem, et basilíscum ambulábis: * et conculcábis leónem et dracónem.
content.english: 90:13 Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: * and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon.

content.latin: 90:14 Quóniam in me sperávit, liberábo eum: * prótegam eum, quóniam cognóvit nomen meum.
content.english: 90:14 Because he hoped in me I will deliver him: * I will protect him because he hath known my name.

content.latin: 90:15 Clamábit ad me, et ego exáudiam eum: * cum ipso sum in tribulatióne: erípiam eum et glorificábo eum.
content.english: 90:15 He shall cry to me, and I will hear him: * I am with him in tribulation, I will deliver him, and I will glorify him.

content.latin: 90:16 Longitúdine diérum replébo eum: * et osténdam illi salutáre meum.
content.english: 90:16 I will fill him with length of days; * and I will shew him my salvation.

content.latin: 133:1 Ecce nunc benedícite Dóminum, * omnes servi Dómini:
content.english: 133:1 Behold now bless ye the Lord, * all ye servants of the Lord:

content.latin: 133:1 Qui statis in domo Dómini, * in átriis domus Dei nostri.
content.english: 133:1 Who stand in the house of the Lord, * in the courts of the house of our God.

content.latin: 133:2 In nóctibus extóllite manus vestras in sancta, * et benedícite Dóminum.
content.english: 133:2 In the nights lift up your hands to the holy places, * and bless ye the Lord.

content.latin: 133:3 Benedícat te Dóminus ex Sion, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
content.english: 133:3 May the Lord out of Sion bless thee, * he that made heaven and earth.

content.english: But thou, O Lord, art among us, and thy name is called upon by us: forsake us not, O Lord our God.

content.english: 2:29 Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, ✠ * according to thy word in peace;

content.latin: 2:30 Quia vidérunt óculi mei * salutáre tuum,
content.english: 2:30 Because my eyes have seen * thy salvation,

content.latin: 2:31 Quod parásti * ante fáciem ómnium populórum,

content.english: 2:32 A light to the revelation of the Gentiles, * and the glory of thy people Israel.

content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Vísita, quǽsumus, Dómine, habitatiónem istam, et omnes insídias inimíci ab ea longe repélle: Ángeli tui sancti hábitent in ea, qui nos in pace custódiant; et benedíctio tua sit super nos semper.
content.english: Visit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this dwelling, and drive far from it the snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to preserve us in peace, and let thy blessing be always upon us.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: Benediction. The almighty and merciful Lord, ✠ the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, bless us and keep us.

content.latin: Salve, Regína, mater misericórdiæ;
content.english: Hail holy Queen, Mother of Mercy,

content.latin: vita, dulcédo et spes nóstra, salve.
content.english: our life, our sweetness, and our hope.

content.latin: Ad te clamámus éxsules fílii Hevæ.
content.english: To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve.

content.latin: Ad te suspirámus geméntes et flentes
content.english: To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping

content.latin: In hac lacrimárum valle.
content.english: In this valley of tears.

content.latin: Eia ergo, advocáta nostra,
content.english: Turn then, most gracious Advocate,

content.latin: illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte.
content.english: thine eyes of mercy toward us.

content.latin: Et Iesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui,
content.english: And after this our exile show unto us

content.latin: nobis post hoc exsílium osténde.
content.english: the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

content.latin: O clemens, o pia, o dulcis Virgo María.
content.english: O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

content.latin: ℣. Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.
content.english: ℣. Pray for us, O Holy Mother of God.

content.latin: ℟. Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
content.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui gloriósæ Vírginis Matris Maríæ corpus et ánimam, ut dignum Fílii tui habitáculum éffici mererétur, Spíritu Sancto cooperánte, præparásti: da, ut, cuius commemoratióne lætámur, eius pia intercessióne, ab instántibus malis et a morte perpétua liberémur. Per eúndem Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
content.english: O almighty, everlasting God, who by the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, didst prepare the body and soul of Mary, glorious Virgin and Mother, to become a worthy dwelling for Thy Son; grant that we who rejoice in her commemoration may, by her gracious intercession, be delivered from present evils and from everlasting death. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.
content.english: ℣. May the divine assistance ✠ remain with us always.
